title: Parking on large conditioned critical Galton–Watson trees with aperiodic finite-variance offspring and finite-variance arrivals of mean at most one has the moment-determined subcritical, critical and linear-flux phase transition
difficulty: After the stated conditioned-tree local/fringe limits, classical spine identity and Wald hitting-time formula, one still has to derive the arrival-time integral equation and rule out premature explosion by finite-height monotone truncations. The main conditioned-tree conclusion additionally requires the explicit three-piece comparison and a locality argument absorbing both upper fluxes into empty lower-spine spots. Those source-local coupled constructions and limit controls are nonroutine, so the full theorem is conservatively H1.

title: For integer linear forms with independent degree s plus one powers, a small Gowers norm of one nonnegative bounded function controls their multilinear average without a flag assumption
difficulty: After the precise arithmetic regularity, flag counting, generalized von Neumann and nilsequence converse prerequisites, the author still supplies the polytope packing and progression-fibre counting that control the outer small-error average. The proof must then combine step-lowering nilmanifold integration with full subprogression Fourier cutoff control and the integer rescaling closing. These remaining uniform estimates and constructions are beyond routine qualification applications, giving a conservative H1 for the selected nonnegative-function scope.

title: A nonnegative integer multiset with two-prime cyclotomic divisors at r distinct positive p-exponents and total weight indivisible by q has at least p to the r elements
difficulty: After the classical cuboid/fibre criterion and the two-prime positive fibre decomposition of Lam--Leung Theorem 3.3, the proof still has to propagate all remaining cyclotomic divisors across successively finer congruence grids. The author uses CRT-normalized fibres to keep every one of the p smaller-grid weights indivisible by q, enabling the exponent-amplifying induction. This simultaneous multiscale preservation and positivity constraint is the concrete nonroutine obligation, so the precise Proposition 5.1 is conservatively H1.
